title: Tethered Reserve Timeline Canvas - compact controls and forecast for Dedicated GPU Pools
creator: Priya Anand
description:
Overview:
Create a compact, timeline-first control surface for Dedicated GPU pools that unifies reserve (committed capacity) configuration, burst controls, and a short-term capacity forecast. This ticket covers the high-fidelity prototype, accessibility pass, and a small interactive handoff kit for engineering to implement the canvas in the Redwood Console.

Background:
Customer signals and support tickets show confusion when managing reserved capacity vs. burst credits. Platform SREs want a single view that shows: current pool health, reserve utilization, burst budget, and a 6-hour forecast with recommended autoscale knobs. The existing dedicated capacity pages are fragmented across three screens (Reserve UI, Pool Health, Burst settings).

Goals:
- Reduce cognitive load for on-call and SRE operators by surfacing the top 3 actions (adjust reserve, configure burst window, enable predictive scale-down) on one canvas.
- Provide a compact timeline that maps traffic spikes to reserve usage and burst consumption with clear cost deltas.
- Include a lightweight decision mode: "Recommend" vs "Manual" with explainable heuristics for predictive settings.
- Keep interactions keyboard-accessible and readable at 12px density for compact dashboards.

Scope and non-goals:
In-scope: single-pool canvas (desktop and large tablet), burst slider + reserve timeline, forecast overlay, cost delta preview, tooltip-based guidance, exportable snapshot for runbooks.
Out-of-scope: multi-pool orchestration views, full RBAC screens, backend autoscaling policy engine (engineers will map controls to existing autoscaler APIs).

Constraints and assumptions:
- Must fit the console's compact panes (minimum width 760px).
- Real-time metrics feed limited to 5s resolution for foreground widgets; historical data uses 1m buckets.
- Forecast algorithm will be provided by Product/ML; prototype uses simulated forecast for handoff.
- Burst budget is additive to reserve; show both absolute and percentage views.
acceptance_criteria: High-fidelity Figma prototype covers desktop and large-tablet breakpoints and is clickable for the reserve timeline and burst slider interactions.
Prototype demonstrates 'Recommend' mode that suggests reserve delta (+/-) with a clear cost delta preview for 24 hours.
Design spec contains accessibility notes for keyboard focus order, aria-labels for timeline markers, and color contrast values for forecasting overlays.
Engineering handoff includes tokens (spacing, typography, color), component variants (compact timeline, slider, pill toggles), and interaction spec with microcopy.
PM and Eng have signed off on the mapping between UI controls and backend autoscaler fields (documented in review comments below).
review_feedback: 2026-03-02 - Jon Park (PM): Recommend mode is valuable, but show explicit signal sources (traffic vs. scheduled jobs) in tooltip.
2026-03-04 - Elena Novak (Eng): Need to confirm that the burst slider maps to both 'burst window' and 'max burst concurrency' fields; otherwise we'll have semantic mismatch.
2026-03-06 - Aisha Carvalho (SRE): Forecast overlay looks good; request a 'confidence' band and a compact explanation for on-call to avoid blind trust.
2026-03-09 - Accessibility review (internal): Color contrast for the forecast orange band at 30% opacity fails; extended palette provided in decisions.
comments: 2026-03-01 Priya Anand: Initial prototype uploaded; focus state and keyboard flows added. Next: incorporate cost delta microcopy and hook up simulated forecast.
2026-03-03 Marco Ruiz: Added engineering notes describing required API surface (autoscaler.reserve_units, autoscaler.burst_window_secs, autoscaler.recommendation_id). Refer to GitHub PR stub.
2026-03-07 Priya Anand: Addressed feedback from SRE - added confidence band, hover explanation for 'recommendation' logic, and example runbook snapshot export button.
2026-03-10 Marco Ruiz: Quick code review of CSS tokens passed; engineering has a blocker for the burst slider animation (will simplify to instant apply).
decisions: Unify reserve and burst controls on a single timeline; do not create separate pages for now to reduce context switching.
Expose two control modes: 'Recommend' (default for post-provisioning) and 'Manual' for advanced operators. 'Recommend' includes a one-click apply and short rationale.
Forecast confidence band will use secondary palette colors with improved contrast (#1F77B4 for high, #FFA726 for medium, #D32F2F for low) and an aria-describedby text element.
Burst slider will only change 'burst_window_secs' and 'burst_unit_limit' fields; 'max_concurrency' will remain a separate numeric input to avoid hidden behavior.
Cost delta preview will show estimated delta for the next 24h and include a link to the Cost Explorer for deeper analysis.
next_steps: Address Elena's engineering mapping question and update the Figma spec by 2026-03-12.
Create a small UX test (5 SRE participants) to validate comprehension of recommend vs manual flows before implementation begins.
Hand off redlines and tokens to Engineering; pair with Marco for initial integration spike (2 days).
Add a follow-up ticket to extend the canvas to multi-pool views in Q2 (scope draft included in PRD).
